item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: In which of these drawings is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Butterfly with a dotted line]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Outline of a human body with a dotted line]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Elephant with a dotted line]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Snake with a dotted line]

item.figure_description:
Four line drawings labeled A, B, C, and D, each with a straight dotted line:
- A: A top-down view of a butterfly, tilted diagonally. The dotted line passes straight through the body from between the antennae to the tail, splitting the butterfly into two symmetric halves.
- B: A front-facing outline of a human body standing upright with arms at the sides. A horizontal dotted line passes across the waist.
- C: A front view of an elephant with its trunk curved slightly to one side, its tail visible on only one side, and asymmetric feet. A vertical dotted line runs down the center of the drawing.
- D: A snake drawn horizontally, stretched out with its head on the right and tail on the left. A vertical dotted line cuts across the snake's body near the middle.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: In which of the following figures is the dotted line a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a square into two opposite trapezoids.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a rectangle into two opposite right angle triangles.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a pentagon into a trapezoid and an irregular pentagon.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a dotted line dividing a hexagon in the middle.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes, each intersected by a dotted line:
- Option A shows a square with a tilted dotted line that enters through the top side near the top-left corner and exits through the bottom side near the bottom-right corner, dividing the square into two non-congruent trapezoids.
- Option B shows a horizontal rectangle with a dotted line running along the diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner.
- Option C shows a regular pentagon with one vertex at the top and a horizontal base at the bottom. A slightly slanted, nearly horizontal dotted line cuts through the left and right sides below the center, dividing it into an upper portion and a lower trapezoid.
- Option D shows a regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges. A vertical dotted line passes through the exact center, bisecting the top and bottom edges into two identical mirror-image halves.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
On the grid below, draw the reflection of the shape in the dotted line of symmetry.

[Image: Grid with a polygon and a dashed line of symmetry]

descriptors: One or more of image lines drawn correctly, but image not completely correct
Attempt to sketch an image under a transformation other than reflection (e.g., translation of image)
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
An 8 by 8 grid of square cells with a vertical dashed line of symmetry running along the central vertical grid line (between the 4th and 5th columns from the left).
To the right of the dashed line is a six-sided polygon with vertices at grid intersections (with column lines 0 to 8 from left to right, and row lines 0 to 8 from top to bottom):
- (column 4, row 3) on the dashed line
- (column 5, row 2)
- (column 6, row 4)
- (column 7, row 4)
- (column 7, row 6)
- (column 4, row 5) on the dashed line

The edges of the polygon connect these vertices in sequence:
- A straight segment from (4, 3) up and right to (5, 2)
- A segment from (5, 2) down and right to (6, 4)
- A horizontal segment from (6, 4) to (7, 4)
- A vertical segment from (7, 4) down to (7, 6)
- A slanted segment from (7, 6) up and left to (4, 5)
- A vertical segment of length 2 along the dashed line from (4, 5) up to (4, 3)
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a complex figure shaped like a bow tie with lines of symmetry shaded on faded square lines.]

How many lines of symmetry does this figure have?
reference_items.figure_description:
A shaded, symmetric bow-tie-shaped polygon is drawn on a grid of squares measuring 6 columns wide and 4 rows high.
- The shape has two vertical outer ends: a left vertical side along the first interior vertical grid line spanning the middle 2 units in height, and an identical right vertical side along the fifth vertical grid line spanning the middle 2 units in height.
- From the top and bottom endpoints of each vertical side, the top and bottom edges slope inward toward a narrower central "neck."
- At the center of the figure, the top and bottom boundaries each form a short horizontal segment parallel to the grid lines.
- The figure is horizontally and vertically symmetric across the central vertical grid line and the central horizontal grid line.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
Draw the line of symmetry on this shape.

[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy-ends at either end.]

descriptors:
Line drawn correctly as shown
[Image: an elongated kite shape figure with two pointy ends at either end. A dotted line goes lengthwise through the figure, through the pointy ends.]
Incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: A quadrilateral kite shape oriented diagonally on a blank background. It has a sharp, acute vertex pointing toward the bottom left. From this vertex, two long straight sides of equal length extend upward and to the right: one side goes steeply up and right to an upper vertex, and the other side goes gently up and right to a lower-right vertex. The top side is a short horizontal segment extending rightward from the upper vertex, and the right side is a short vertical segment extending upward from the lower-right vertex, meeting at a top-right corner.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a rectangle shape with a line connected to a dot on the left side pointing down.]
Which of the following shows the position of the shape above after a half turn or 180° rotation?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a rectangle shape with a line connected to a dot pointing left.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a rectangle shape with a line connected to a dot pointing up.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a rectangle shape with a line connected to a dot pointing right.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a rectangle shape with a line connected to a dot pointing down.]

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top is a figure consisting of a horizontal rectangle (wider than it is tall) with a straight line segment extending vertically downward from its lower-left corner, ending with a solid black dot.
Four options show rotations or positions of the shape:
- Option A shows a vertical rectangle (taller than it is wide) with a line segment extending horizontally to the left from its upper-left corner, ending with a solid dot.
- Option B shows a horizontal rectangle with a line segment extending vertically upward from its upper-right corner, ending with a solid dot.
- Option C shows a vertical rectangle with a line segment extending horizontally to the right from its lower-right corner, ending with a solid dot.
- Option D shows a horizontal rectangle identical to the original figure, with a line segment extending downward from the lower-left corner, ending with a solid dot.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

[Image: an incomplete shape with three sides forming a rectangle on a grid.]

descriptors:
Correct shape drawn which has 5 sides and 1 line of symmetry. The new vertex must be within ±2 mm of the line of symmetry (accept the new vertex anywhere on the line of symmetry, provided there are 5 sides).
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.] OR
[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. Two lines sloping inwards are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]

[Image: figure drawn on grid with three lines forming an incomplete rectangle on the bottom. The rectangle is completed with a fourth line and then two additional lines are drawn on top to close the figure and form a convex interior angle.]
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: A 10 by 10 square grid. A three-sided incomplete shape is drawn with thick black lines along the grid lines: a horizontal bottom segment 6 units long (leaving 2 units of margin on the left and 2 units on the right along the bottom edge of the grid), and two vertical segments each 4 units tall rising upward from the two ends of the bottom segment (leaving 6 units of grid space above them). The top of the shape is open.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jill had a rectangular piece of paper.

[Image: A rectangle divided horizontally into two equal halves by a dotted line]

She cut her paper along the dotted line and made an L shape like this.

[Image: An L-shaped figure made of two rectangular strips]

Which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The area of the L shape is greater than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: B
options.text: The area of the L shape is equal to the area of the rectangle.

options.label: C
options.text: The area of the L shape is less than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot work out which area is greater without measuring.

reference_items.figure_description:
The first figure shows a horizontal rectangle with a dashed horizontal line dividing it into two equal top and bottom halves.

The second figure shows an L shape made from the two halves: one vertical rectangular strip on the left and one horizontal rectangular strip at the bottom right, joined along part of their edges at a right angle.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
Four square boxes labeled A, B, C, and D, each containing black (filled) and white (open) circles:
- Option A: Contains 4 circles in a 2 by 2 arrangement. Top row: 1 black circle, 1 white circle. Bottom row: 2 white circles.
- Option B: Contains 6 circles in 2 rows of 3. Top row: white, black, white. Bottom row: black, black, white.
- Option C: Contains 3 circles. Top row: white on the left, black on the right. Bottom row: black on the left.
- Option D: Contains 5 circles arranged in an X pattern like the five dots on a die. Top-left is black, top-right is white, center is white, bottom-left is white, and bottom-right is black.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
These shapes are arranged in a pattern.

[Image: Pattern of shapes]

Which set of shapes is arranged in the same pattern?
reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem, a horizontal sequence of shapes shows: 1 open circle, 1 open triangle, 2 open circles, 2 open triangles, 3 open circles, 3 open triangles.
Option A shows a horizontal sequence: 1 solid star, 1 open square, 1 solid star, 1 open square, 2 solid stars, 2 open squares, 2 solid stars, 2 open squares.
Option B shows a horizontal sequence: 1 open square, 1 solid star, 2 open squares, 1 solid star, 3 open squares, 1 solid star, 4 open squares.
Option C shows a horizontal sequence: 1 solid star, 1 open square, 2 solid stars, 2 open squares, 3 solid stars, 3 open squares.
Option D shows a horizontal sequence: 2 open squares, 2 solid stars, 1 open square, 1 solid star, 2 open squares, 2 solid stars, 1 open square, 1 solid star.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
